acceptance: The gate verdict does not depend on one run's calibration outlier, or the normalization limits are documented with a worked example.
context: 2026-11-11: merged duplicate ci-fast-duration-gate-slow-runner-margin-20261101 into this item. Slow-runner evidence from that item: of 59 post-flip verdicts, 15 ran with a runner speed factor >= 1.5 (up to 1.95) and 8 had a summed ratio above 1.20 (max 1.282 vs the 1.30 limit); 7 of 59 exceeded the 360 s delta term alone. #4002 (deleting tests only) got would-block at 1.313 / +442.6 s with a median per-test ratio of 1.010. Acceptance should cover both a false would-block on a slow runner and a real slowdown hidden by a slow runner.
description: For core PR 3562 the fast-tier verdict was would-block with a normalized summed ratio of 1.156 although the PR's own tests added 0.08s. The run's calibration factor was 1.84, most excess was first-in-worker import cost spread over unrelated tests, and an offline verify of the old head's artifact against a freshly built baseline raised the ratio to 1.196. The baseline was regenerated to lift the refusal, which hides the cause.
